content:
This is your sketch, not your statement — but even a sketch this rough tells me something worth acting on.

Your ≈£4,050/mo free cash looks healthy until you hold it against the goal. The deposit needs ≈£6,670/mo — that's ≈108% of your take-home. The timeline as you've described it doesn't close on its own. What it does have is ≈£3,270/mo of drift: free cash that isn't eating out, isn't saving, and isn't explained by your fixed base of ≈£2,150/mo.

The move: set up a standing transfer of ≈£300/mo on payday. That's sized at roughly half the drift — enough to land without biting. At that pace, the deposit arrives in ≈25 months instead of ≈40.

You called the ≈£3,270/mo drift worth it. That may be exactly right. A real month settles whether it's genuinely accounted for, or whether some of it is just invisible spend that hasn't had a name put on it yet.

Checking a real month does two things. It swaps every ≈ for an actual number — estimate and reality side by side. And the habits half of this picture is still empty: timing, patterns, what's recurring. Estimates can't see any of that. Only real transactions can.

Right now, I know you about 56%. Checking a real month is what takes that past 70%.

[CTA:start_statement_check]Check my numbers[/CTA]

— C.
